pages.title: ascend-ci-deployment - 项目概览
pages.content:
# ascend-ci-deployment

This repository is used to deploy Actions Runner Controller on a Kubernetes cluster with Ascend NPU chips, enabling organizations and repositories to integrate Ascend CI. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

**语言**：gotmpl, json, markdown, python, shell, tgz, tpl, txt, unknown, yaml
**框架/依赖**：Helm, Kustomize, GitHub Actions

pages.title: 项目导览
pages.content:
# 项目导览

## 1. Project Overview

README.md explains this repo's purpose: it stores Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, and Kustomize overlays used to deploy the GitHub Actions Runner Controller (ARC) on Ascend NPU clusters. It lays out the top-level structure -- projects/, other/, monitoring/, manifests/, and argocd/ -- that every subsequent step in this tour will explore. Since this is a GitOps configuration repo rather than a running application, there is no code entry point; this directory map is the true 'front door'.

相关节点：document:README.md

## 2. Anatomy of an Active Project: vllm-ascend Config

projects/{org}/{repo}/config/ is the base Kustomize overlay every active CI project ships. Its kustomization.yaml bundles the namespace, GitHub token secret, local-storage PVC, and RBAC permissions into one deployable unit for the vllm-project/vllm-ascend runner. This is the template that every new active project in projects/ follows.

> 语言要点：Kustomize kustomization.yaml files declare a set of resource files to compose without templating -- overlays layer changes (like a cluster-specific namespace) on top of a shared base, letting many clusters reuse the same core manifests.

相关节点：config:projects/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/config/kustomization.yaml, config:projects/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/config/namespace.yaml

## 3. Secrets, Storage, and Permissions

Building on Step 2's kustomization, the individual resources it bundles reveal the recurring building blocks of a runner config: github-token-secret.yaml syncs a Vault-managed GitHub token into a Kubernetes Secret, local-storage-pvc.yaml requests SFS Turbo shared storage for the runner's workspace, and runner-pod-permission.yaml grants the ServiceAccount the RBAC it needs to manage its own pods. Every project directory in this repo repeats this same trio of concerns.

相关节点：config:projects/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/config/github-token-secret.yaml, config:projects/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/config/local-storage-pvc.yaml, config:projects/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/config/runner-pod-permission.yaml

## 4. Runner Scale Sets as Helm Charts

Once the base config from Steps 2-3 is in place, the actual GitHub Actions runners are deployed as Helm releases of the gha-runner-scale-set chart. linux-aarch64-310p-1/values.yaml configures a runner requiring a single Ascend-310 NPU, pointing githubConfigUrl at the target repository and wiring in the secret and PVC from the previous step. The directory naming convention -- linux-{arch}-{npu}-{count} -- directly encodes the hardware a given runner scale set consumes.

> 语言要点：Helm values.yaml files parameterize a chart's templates. Here the same gha-runner-scale-set chart is instantiated many times with different values -- once per NPU count -- rather than duplicating template logic.

相关节点：config:projects/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/linux-aarch64-310p-1/values.yaml

## 5. Shared Cluster Resources Behind the Scenes

Many project configs reference common, reusable building blocks rather than defining everything from scratch. shared-configmap-pattern and shared-pvc-pattern are logical resources with high fan-in, representing the pod-template ConfigMap and PVC conventions reused across dozens of projects, while the runner-containers-hooks image is the container image nearly every runner scale set pulls. Recognizing these shared patterns explains why Steps 2-4's structure repeats almost identically across the whole repo.

相关节点：config:shared-configmap-pattern, config:shared-pvc-pattern, resource:image:runner-containers-hooks:release-2.336-6e2e20

## 6. Legacy Projects Under other/

Not every project stays under projects/ -- once a project's CI activity drops, its runner config moves to other/{org}/{repo}/ while keeping the exact same internal structure as Steps 2-4. other/ascend-gha-runners/vllm-ascend/config-cn12-001/kustomization.yaml shows this: it is a cluster-specific overlay (the config-{cluster} naming variant) for a maintenance-mode deployment, proving that projects/ vs other/ is purely about activity level, not a difference in architecture.

相关节点：config:other/ascend-gha-runners/vllm-ascend/config-cn12-001/kustomization.yaml

## 7. The ARC Controller Itself

Everything in Steps 2-6 depends on the gha-runner-scale-set-controller operator being installed first -- that's what manifests/arc-controller-0.14.2/ provides. Its Chart.yaml declares the controller's Helm chart dependency, while values.yaml configures the custom SWR-hosted controller image, resource limits, and CRDs that every runner scale set in the cluster relies on. Different clusters run different controller versions (0.13.0 vs 0.14.2), which is why the repo maintains multiple manifests/arc-controller-* directories side by side.

相关节点：config:manifests/arc-controller-0.14.2/Chart.yaml, config:manifests/arc-controller-0.14.2/values.yaml

## 8. Wiring It Together with ArgoCD

None of the manifests from Steps 2-7 apply themselves -- ArgoCD Applications under argocd/clusters/{cluster}/ are what actually sync them to a live cluster. vllm-ascend-vllm-ascend-recipes-config.yaml is a Config Application pointing its source.path at a projects/ Kustomize overlay like the one from Step 2, with CreateNamespace=true and automated pruning enabled so the cluster state always matches the repo. This is the GitOps loop that ties the whole directory structure to real infrastructure.

> 语言要点：Kubernetes: ArgoCD Applications are themselves a CRD that describes a desired sync between a Git path and a cluster/namespace. `automated.prune: true` means resources deleted from Git are also deleted from the live cluster, keeping infrastructure state and repo state identical.

相关节点：config:argocd/clusters/ascend-infra-guiyang-cluster-001/vllm-ascend-vllm-ascend-recipes-config.yaml

## 9. Autoscaling Job Load: the NPU Scheduler

With runners, controller, and ArgoCD sync all in place, the npu-scheduler pipeline resource represents the logic that governs how CI job load actually gets matched to available NPU-equipped nodes across the fleet of runner scale sets built in earlier steps. Its high fan-in reflects how central it is to keeping runner utilization efficient across all the projects covered so far.

相关节点：pipeline:npu-scheduler

## 10. Monitoring the Fleet

monitoring/ sits at the top level, outside both projects/ and other/, because it watches every cluster rather than belonging to any one org. monitoring/base/kustomization.yaml assembles the monitoring namespace, RBAC, and secrets; the prometheus-agent-deployment.yaml runs Prometheus in agent mode to scrape and remote_write metrics without local querying; and cronjob-github-probe.yaml is one of several scheduled health checks (GitHub reachability, cert expiry, disk usage) that keep the runner infrastructure observable.

相关节点：config:monitoring/base/kustomization.yaml, service:monitoring/base/prometheus-agent-deployment.yaml, pipeline:monitoring/base/cronjob-github-probe.yaml

## 11. Validating Changes Before They Merge

Because every change to the patterns from Steps 2-8 flows through a Pull Request, ci-lint.yml is the GitHub Actions workflow that lints changed YAML and validates ArgoCD Application manifests on every push. It calls out to repo-level scripts -- argocd-app-lint.sh checks Application YAML against the conventions from Step 8, and check-projects-coverage.py verifies that any newly added project directory actually gets a matching ArgoCD Application, closing the loop between the two halves of the repo.

> 语言要点：YAML (CI/CD): GitHub Actions workflows use `on` triggers (here, push/PR) and `jobs`/`steps` to run validation scripts sequentially, catching malformed manifests before they reach ArgoCD's automated sync.

相关节点：pipeline:.github/workflows/ci-lint.yml, file:scripts/argocd-app-lint.sh, file:scripts/check-projects-coverage.py

## 12. Scaffolding New Deployments with Agent Skills

To keep new projects consistent with everything covered in this tour, the repo ships a Claude Agent skill: arc-deploy/SKILL.md documents a workflow that generates namespace, secret, PVC, ConfigMap, and Helm values files from a JSON template. sfsturbo.json is a generic template demonstrating the SFS Turbo storage settings from Step 3, showing how the manual pattern from Steps 2-4 has been captured as reusable tooling.

相关节点：document:.claude/skills/arc-deploy/SKILL.md, config:.claude/skills/arc-deploy/templates/sfsturbo.json

## 13. Repository Conventions and CI Checks

Finally, docs/ci-checks.md and CLAUDE.md document the conventions this whole tour has traced in practice: directory placement rules, naming schemes for namespaces and runner scale sets, and the mandatory branch-protection and PR-with-linked-issue workflow. Reading these alongside the CI validation from Step 11 gives a complete picture of how the repo enforces the architecture explored from Step 2 onward.

相关节点：document:docs/ci-checks.md, document:CLAUDE.md

pages.title: argocd-app-lint.sh
pages.content:
Shell lint script that validates ArgoCD Application YAML files against repository conventions, checking metadata naming, source path correspondence, and other structural rules (r1-r7 checks).

语言/实现要点：Pure Bash with modular rule-check functions (r1_check..r7_check) each validating one repo convention; no tree-sitter grammar support so structure was extracted via top-level NAME() {...} pattern matching.

pages.title: extract_metadata_names
pages.content: Extracts metadata.name values from ArgoCD Application YAML documents for downstream comparison checks.

pages.title: extract_source_paths
pages.content: Extracts spec.source(s).path values from an Application YAML document to verify they match repository directory layout.

pages.title: has_single_source_missing_path
pages.content: Detects Application documents with a single-source spec that is missing a required source path field.

pages.title: names_correspond
pages.content: Checks whether an Application's metadata name corresponds to its derived source path per naming convention.

pages.title: r1_check
pages.content: Implements repository rule R1, reporting lint failures for Application files that violate the first naming/structure convention.

pages.title: r2_check
pages.content: Implements repository rule R2, validating Application source path conventions and reporting violations.

pages.title: r4_check
pages.content: Implements repository rule R4, a larger structural validation over Application YAML documents with multiple sub-checks and failure reporting.

pages.title: r5_check
pages.content: Implements repository rule R5, validating additional Application manifest conventions and reporting lint failures.

pages.title: r6_check
pages.content: Implements repository rule R6, validating Application manifest conventions and reporting lint failures.

pages.title: r7_check
pages.content: Implements repository rule R7, the final and most extensive lint check over Application YAML documents.

pages.title: check-projects-coverage.py
pages.content: CI script that compares newly added project directories (via git diff against a merge-base) with ArgoCD Application source paths and documented runner names, reporting coverage mismatches for the repo docs/table.

pages.title: report_fail
pages.content: Records and prints a lint failure with rule id, path, and message, and sets the module-level failed flag.

pages.title: get_new_project_dirs
pages.content: Uses git merge-base and git diff to determine newly added directories under projects/ in the current change set.

pages.title: _load_yaml_docs
pages.content: Loads all YAML documents from a file path, returning None on read/parse failure.

pages.title: all_app_source_paths
pages.content: Walks the ArgoCD Application directory tree and collects all spec.source(s).path values referenced by Application manifests, keyed by path with the referencing files.

pages.title: fetch_docs_runner_names
pages.content: Fetches the docs table listing documented runner project names via a GitHub API request and parses the markdown table rows.

pages.title: extract_scale_set_labels
pages.content: Reads a runner Helm values.yaml file and extracts the gha-runner-scale-set.scaleSetLabels values.

pages.title: main
pages.content: Entry point orchestrating the coverage check: finds new project dirs, cross-references Application source paths and docs runner names, and reports failures via report_fail, exiting non-zero on violations.

pages.title: test-argocd-app-lint.sh
pages.content:
Shell test suite for scripts/argocd-app-lint.sh, building temporary sample repos and asserting pass/fail lint behavior across the script's rule checks.

语言/实现要点：Bash test harness with assert_pass/assert_fail_with helpers and a setup_valid_repo fixture builder; no tree-sitter grammar for shell so structure came from top-level NAME() {...} pattern matching.

pages.title: assert_pass
pages.content: Test assertion helper that runs the lint script against a fixture and expects a successful (passing) exit.

pages.title: assert_fail_with
pages.content: Test assertion helper that runs the lint script against a fixture and expects failure containing a specific message/rule.

pages.title: setup_valid_repo
pages.content: Fixture builder that scaffolds a temporary directory tree with valid ArgoCD Application/config files used as the baseline for lint test cases.

pages.title: test_check_projects_coverage.py
pages.content: Pytest suite for scripts/check-projects-coverage.py, covering YAML doc loading, Application source-path extraction, and failure-reporting behavior.

pages.title: _reset_failed
pages.content: Test helper that resets the module-level failed flag on the check-projects-coverage module between test cases.

pages.title: TestLoadYamlDocs
pages.content: Test class covering _load_yaml_docs behavior for single-doc, multi-doc, invalid, and missing-file YAML inputs.

pages.title: TestAllAppSourcePaths
pages.content: Test class covering all_app_source_paths behavior across single/multi-source specs, multidoc YAML, non-Application docs, and unreadable YAML files, using an _write_app fixture helper.

pages.title: TestReportFail
pages.content: Test class covering report_fail's flag-setting behavior, printed output, and accumulation of multiple failures.

pages.title: test_sync_new_projects_to_docs.py
pages.content: Pytest suite exercising a docs-sync module's add_to_repo_md and add_to_repos_txt helpers, verifying row insertion, formatting, and fallback behavior for the projects documentation table.

pages.title: TestAddToRepoMd
pages.content: Test class covering add_to_repo_md's row insertion before an end marker, row formatting, fallback when no marker exists, and duplicate-avoidance.

pages.title: TestAddToReposTxt
pages.content: Test class covering add_to_repos_txt's entry appending, preservation of existing entries, trailing newline handling, and separator formatting.
